ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, a ship is located at point $A$, which is at the northeast direction $45^\circ$ from the lighthouse $C$ and at a distance of $60$ nautical miles from it. After sailing southward for a while, it arrives at point $B$, which is at the southeast direction $30^\circ$ from the lighthouse $C$. What is the distance between the ship and the lighthouse $C$ at this point? (Keep the square root in the result.)
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Draw CD $\perp$ AB. In the right triangle $ACD$, $\angle A=45^\circ$ and AC=60 nautical miles,\\
$\therefore \triangle ACD$ is an isosceles right triangle,\\
$\therefore$ AD=CD=$\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}$AC=30$\sqrt{2}$ nautical miles,\\
In right triangle $BCD$, $\angle B=30^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ BC=2CD=2×30$\sqrt{2}$=60$\sqrt{2}$ nautical miles\\
Thus, at this time, the distance from the ship to the lighthouse is \boxed{60\sqrt{2}} nautical miles.

Thus, the distance from the ship to the lighthouse is $60\sqrt{2}$ nautical miles.
ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, there is a vertical dashed line passing through point C, representing the north-south direction; point A is located to the upper right of C, and point B is located to the lower right of C; A and B are connected by a vertical solid line, representing the ship going straight south from A to B, so A and B have the same eastward distance. The angle between segment CA and the vertical direction is marked as 45°, and the angle between segment CB and the vertical direction is marked as 30°. Reasoning: Take lighthouse C as the origin, east as the positive direction of the x-axis, and north as the positive direction of the y-axis. It is known that AC=60, and A is in the northeast 45° direction from C, so A's eastward coordinate is 60 sin45°=60·√2/2=30√2. Because B is due south of A, and AB is vertical, B's eastward coordinate is also equal to 30√2. Also because B is in the southeast 30° direction from C, if BC is the distance sought, then B's eastward coordinate is BC sin30°. Therefore BC sin30°=30√2, that is, BC·1/2=30√2, solving gives BC=60√2.
